title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-10-28

hits.name: Watcher.Guru
hits.text: JUST IN: Google unveils new security system to help banks safely store and transfer cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets.
hits.hook: JUST IN: Google unveils new security system to help banks safely store and transfer cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets.
hits.story: Google builds crypto custody system for banks
hits.draft_en:
Google is building tech for banks to store and move crypto.

Big name. For $BTC holders the useful question is simple:

who holds the keys?

If it's the bank, it's a better vault.
Not self-custody.

Both can exist. Just don't confuse them.

Bank on Google's rails, or your own keys?
Save this for the next 'big tech adopts Bitcoin' headline.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Better institutional custody helps adoption. It's still custody: someone else holds the keys.

What's the actual model, MPC, HSMs, who signs? Those details decide whether it's progress or a new single point of failure.
hits.video_tip: Vault with a big-tech lock vs a hardware wallet in a hand, caption 'who holds the keys?'. 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask who holds and signs with the keys (bank, Google, MPC split?) and note institutional custody isn't self-custody; check the technical details before calling it adoption.
hits.why_chosen: Top fresh custody headline with zero details; perfect for a 'who holds the keys' question.

hits.name: Michael Saylor
hits.text: $MSTR shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor. The amendment enables $STRF, $STRC, $STRK and $STRD to accrue dividends every calendar day. Thank you to all who voted. https://t.co/w1Cp4GKUy5
hits.hook: $MSTR shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor. The amendment enables $STRF, $STRC, $STRK and $STRD to accrue dividends ever
hits.story: Strategy preferreds get daily dividends
hits.draft_en:
Strategy's preferred stocks will now accrue dividends every day, after a 99.3% shareholder vote (preliminary).

Worth being clear on what that is:
- a claim on a company that holds $BTC
- paid in dollars, by that company
- not bitcoin, and not your keys

Yield always comes from somewhere.
Here it's the issuer's ability to keep paying.

Would you hold the preferred or the coin?
Save this before someone calls it 'Bitcoin yield'.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Daily accrual changes the payment schedule, not the source of the payment.

Honest question: what happens to these dividends in a long $BTC drawdown? Has anyone modeled the coverage?
hits.video_tip: Split screen: a coin in a hardware wallet vs. a share certificate, caption 'which one is bitcoin?'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Separate the instrument from the asset: a preferred is a company's dollar obligation; ask how coverage holds up in a deep $BTC drawdown (check the filings).
hits.why_chosen: Huge reach with a product most readers confuse with holding BTC; room for a clear custody/risk distinction.

hits.name: Bitcoin Magazine
hits.text: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen inflows of $286.3 million so far this week 🚀 https://t.co/DPzrElmcdL
hits.hook: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen inflows of $286.3 million so far this week 🚀 https://t.co/DPzrElmcdL
hits.draft_en:
$286.3M into US spot $BTC ETFs so far this week, per Bitcoin Magazine.

Inflows are a fact. 'Bullish' is the interpretation.

Two things I'd check before calling it demand:
- how concentrated it is (Tuesday: IBIT took $151.5M of $176M, per The Block)
- whether flows like this led price in past weeks, or followed it

Do flows lead $BTC, or chase it?
Repost if a friend reads every inflow as a buy signal.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Weekly inflows are real data. The open question is whether they lead $BTC price or chase it.

Anyone run weekly flows vs next-week returns since launch? That's the test, not the rocket emoji.
hits.video_tip: Weekly ETF flow bars with the price line on top, caption 'lead or lag?'. 9s.
hits.reply_angle: Lead or lag: suggest checking weekly spot ETF net flows vs next-week $BTC returns since launch, and how concentrated the flows are in IBIT.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + weekly US spot BTC ETF net flows (bars) vs BTC weekly close (line) since launch, from Farside or issuer data to be checked. Navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Fresh in-lane flow number with hype framing; easy to add concentration and lead/lag questions.

hits.name: Cointelegraph
hits.text:
🚨 ALERT: CZ warns leaked exchange data can fuel phishing, SIM swaps and real-world attacks after four reported leaks across crypto and TradFi.

"Stay SAFU." https://t.co/b9zBTEW7ru
hits.hook: 🚨 ALERT: CZ warns leaked exchange data can fuel phishing, SIM swaps and real-world attacks after four reported leaks across crypto and TradFi.
hits.draft_en:
CZ: leaked exchange data can fuel phishing, SIM swaps and real-world attacks. Four leaks reported across crypto and TradFi.

The part people skip:
your coins can be safe and you can still be a target.

KYC data doesn't expire. Once it leaks, it's out.

What you can control:
- separate email for exchanges
- no SMS 2FA
- withdraw what you don't trade

What would you add?
Repost so someone turns off SMS 2FA today.
hits.draft_quote_en:
'Stay SAFU' is advice. The structural problem is that exchanges hold data you can't rotate like a password.

How many of these leaks came from vendors, not the exchange itself? Coinbase's latest was via Amplitude. Worth tracking.
hits.video_tip: ID card sliding out of an exchange icon into a phishing email. 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Point out leaked KYC data can't be rotated and suggest checking how many recent leaks came through third-party vendors (e.g. Coinbase via Amplitude).
hits.why_chosen: Security warning with a practical gap; invites a checklist reply.

hits.story: Argentine peso at a new low
hits.draft_en:
Argentine peso at a new low against the dollar, per Coin Bureau.
In 2016, $1 bought about 15 pesos. Today, about 1,538.

That's the real case for saving in something you can't print.

But be honest about the trade-off:
- the dollar was the escape hatch for most Argentines
- $BTC adds volatility on top (check 2022)

If you live in a weak-currency country, what did you actually do?
Repost if someone in LatAm needs this framing.
hits.draft_quote_en:
The numbers are worth checking against official and parallel rates, they differ a lot in Argentina.

The real question for a saver there: dollars, $BTC, or both, and in what mix?
hits.video_tip: Peso stack shrinking year by year from 2016 to today, end on a dollar bill and a $BTC logo side by side; 12s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Verify the official vs. parallel rate behind the 99% figure and compare the peso's loss with $BTC's past drawdowns measured in pesos.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + USD/ARS since 2016 (official and parallel rates) next to $BTC priced in ARS; data from official sources and price history, to be checked. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: LatAm currency story close to his audience; numbers to verify and a real savings trade-off.

hits.name: Jack Mallers
hits.text:
My dad always said: for everything in life, even gold, more demand finds more supply.

He was right. Until bitcoin. https://t.co/39k7B5kICT
hits.hook: My dad always said: for everything in life, even gold, more demand finds more supply.
hits.story: More demand, more supply, except bitcoin
hits.draft_en:
'More demand finds more supply. Even gold. Until bitcoin.'

The supply side is true: 21M cap, issuance set in code.

But fixed supply doesn't fix the price.
With supply fixed, demand swings hit price directly.
That's part of why $BTC drawdowns are so deep.

Scarcity is the feature. Volatility is the cost.
Are you sized for both?
If it was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Fixed supply, agreed.

The other side: when demand drops, supply can't adjust either. Fixed supply means demand alone sets the price, both ways.
hits.video_tip: Gold mine output rising vs. a flat 21M line, then a price line swinging; 12s.
hits.reply_angle: Add the missing half: inelastic supply means demand shocks go straight to price; point to past $BTC drawdowns as the cost of scarcity.
hits.why_chosen: Clean scarcity claim with good saves; room to add the volatility side.

hits.name: CoinMarketCap
hits.text: LATEST: ⚡ Stacks founder Muneeb Ali says quantum fears have already put a "ceiling on the growth of Bitcoin," as risk-averse institutions may delay big purchases until a credible upgrade path emerges. https://t.co/kGLsypJQi8
hits.hook: LATEST: ⚡ Stacks founder Muneeb Ali says quantum fears have already put a "ceiling on the growth of Bitcoin," as risk-averse institutions may delay big purchases until a credible upgrade path emerges.
hits.story: Quantum fears and BTC upgrade path
hits.draft_en:
"Quantum fears put a ceiling on $BTC."

That's a claim about buyers, not physics.

Two separate questions:
1. Can a quantum computer break exposed keys today?
2. Are institutions actually delaying buys because of it?

The second one is testable. Has anyone shown the data?
Repost if this question deserves better answers.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Interesting claim. Where's the evidence that institutions are delaying purchases because of quantum, and not because of price, regulation or mandates?

A ceiling should show up somewhere. ETF flows? Allocation filings?
hits.video_tip: Two cards: 'technical risk' vs 'market narrative', ask which one moves price. 12s.
hits.reply_angle: Separate threat from narrative: check whether ETF flows or allocation filings show any quantum-linked delay before accepting a 'ceiling'.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [explanatory image] + two-column card 'Quantum: technical risk vs buyer narrative', what's known vs what's claimed; no figures. Navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Debatable claim with no data attached; room to ask for evidence.

hits.text: $85K keeps turning $BTC back.  Since January, Bitcoin has closed above it on only five days, never more than three in a row. It's a truly tough level to break. More in depth analysis in our latest Week on Chain report https://t.co/xy8lE3ilt3
hits.hook: $85K keeps turning $BTC back.  Since January, Bitcoin has closed above it on only five days, never more than three in a row. It's a truly tough level to break. More in depth analysis in our latest Wee
hits.draft_en:
$85K keeps rejecting $BTC.

glassnode: since January, only five daily closes above it, never more than three in a row.

That's a fact about the past. Not a forecast.

What would change my read:
- a weekly close above it
- holding it on a retest

Buying spot below it, or waiting for the break?
Bookmark this and check it next time $85K gets tested.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Five closes above $85K since January is a clean stat. Next question: how many false breaks came before past multi-month $BTC ceilings finally gave way?

Resistance tells you where. Not when.
hits.video_tip: Daily chart with the $85K line, five dots on the closes above it, then 'day 4?'. 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Base-rate check: ask how many false breaks preceded past multi-month $BTC ceilings and whether a weekly close is better confirmation than a daily one.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + BTC daily closes since January with the $85K line and the five closes above it marked; real price data only. Navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Concrete level stat from an on-chain source, very fresh; invites a spot plan and a false-break question.

$1M FROM FRED KRUEGER

hits.hook: JUST IN: ALL-IN PODCAST CO-HOST JASON CALACANIS JUST GOT CHALLENGED TO $3,000,000 IN COMBINED BETS AFTER SAYING "#BITCOIN WILL NEVER BREAK ITS ALL-TIME HIGH AGAIN"
hits.story: Calacanis challenged to $3M in bets that $BTC never makes a new ATH
hits.draft_en:
Calacanis says $BTC never makes a new all-time high.
Three people offered him $1M bets each. Per the post, he declined.

A bet is the honest version of a prediction.
It forces a date, a level and a cost for being wrong.

Most price calls have none of the three.

What would make you take the other side of a 10-year bet?
If this helps cut through price calls, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Refusing a bet doesn't make him wrong, and offering one doesn't make the bulls right.

But it does show who priced their view. What are the exact terms: level, date, and what counts as a new ATH?
hits.video_tip: Split screen: 'opinion' vs 'bet' with date, level and cost filling in on the bet side; 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Frame it as skin in the game: a prediction with a date, a level and a cost vs a vibe; ask for the exact bet terms (check the original posts) instead of cheering either side.
hits.why_chosen: Viral debate with clear sides; room to add a prediction-market angle without picking a team.

hits.name: CoinDesk
hits.text: MARKETS: Traders now see an 86% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, up from 78% yesterday and 76% last week, according to CME FedWatch.
hits.hook: MARKETS: Traders now see an 86% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, up from 78% yesterday and 76% last week, according to CME FedWatch.
hits.story: Odds of a December Fed hike jump to 86%
hits.draft_en:
Fed held today. Futures now price a December hike at 86%, per CME FedWatch via CoinDesk.

That number moved from 76% to 86% in a week.

Two questions before reading anything into it for $BTC:
- how often were these odds right one or two months out?
- did $BTC actually react to past hike surprises, or just to the noise around them?

Odds are a price, not a promise.

What would change your spot plan, the hike or the surprise?
Save this for the December meeting.
hits.draft_quote_en:
86% a month and a half out is a strong prior, not a done deal.

How often have FedWatch odds this high this early been wrong? That hit rate matters more than the headline number.
hits.video_tip: Line of hike odds over the last week (76% to 86%) with the next FOMC date marked; 10s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Add the base rate: how often FedWatch odds at this level about six weeks out matched the final decision (check CME history), and whether $BTC moved more on surprises than on expected hikes.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + CME FedWatch December hike probability over the last two weeks (76%, 78%, 86% from the post; full series to be checked), with today's FOMC hold marked. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Fresh market-implied probability with a clear trend; perfect for a prediction-market base-rate reply.

hits.name: Bitcoin News
hits.text:
THREE NEW BITCOIN CORE VULNERABILITIES DISCOVERED, INCLUDING BUG ALLOWING ATTACKERS TO REMOTELY CRASH NODES

One flaw lets malicious peers crash Bitcoin nodes running Windows, macOS, or BSD by exhausting memory. Linux nodes are unaffected by this attack.

Another allows attackers https://t.co/oHNWEIwSq8
hits.hook: THREE NEW BITCOIN CORE VULNERABILITIES DISCOVERED, INCLUDING BUG ALLOWING ATTACKERS TO REMOTELY CRASH NODES
hits.story: Three Bitcoin Core vulnerabilities disclosed
hits.draft_en:
Three Bitcoin Core vulnerabilities disclosed, one lets malicious peers crash some nodes, per BitcoinNews.com.

If you run a node, the practical part:
- check which versions are affected
- update from the official release
- verify the signatures before installing

Public disclosure after a fix is how open source is supposed to work.
The risk is people who never update.

When did you last update your node?
Save this for your next node maintenance.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Useful to know which versions are affected and whether the fixes are already in a release.

Any link to the official disclosure? That's what node runners should read, not the headline.
hits.video_tip: Terminal screen: version check, update, signature verification, done; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Point people to the official Bitcoin Core disclosure: affected versions, fixed release, and verifying signatures before updating (check the release notes).
hits.why_chosen: Security news with a concrete action for node runners; fits his autonomy and verification angle.

hits.name: BitQuant
hits.text: $82K is a clear “Buy” signal for bitcoin:native , just as $63K was. https://t.co/fJIQ0D5OX4 https://t.co/r5IKEAEUdz
hits.hook: $82K is a clear “Buy” signal for bitcoin:native , just as $63K was. https://t.co/fJIQ0D5OX4 https://t.co/r5IKEAEUdz
hits.draft_en:
"$82K is a buy signal, just like $63K was."

Maybe.

But a signal that's only shown when it worked isn't a signal yet.

What I'd want to see:
- every time it fired
- how many times it failed
- the drawdown after each one

Spot only, no leverage, and the misses on the table.

Would you buy $BTC on this?
Bookmark it for when the next 'clear buy' shows up.
hits.draft_quote_en:
$63K worked. What about the times it fired and didn't?

Show me the full list of signals, hits and misses, and the max drawdown after each. Then it's a signal.
hits.video_tip: Chart with green 'buy' dots, then grey dots fade in for the misses. 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Survivorship check: ask for every past firing of the signal, including misses and drawdowns, before treating $82K as a buy.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + BTC price with every past firing of the cited buy signal marked, hits and misses, plus drawdown after each; data to be checked from the source. Navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Bold 'clear buy' call with only one past example; strong room for a hit-rate question.

hits.name: Natalie Brunell ⚡️
hits.hook: “Bitcoin would be thrown into total disarray...”
hits.story: AI vs. quantum risk to public keys
hits.draft_en:
AI breaking public key encryption vs. quantum risk: nic_carter's take is getting shared today.

Before panicking, separate the questions:
- what is actually broken today?
- which coins have exposed public keys?
- what would an upgrade path look like?

The practical part: reused or old addresses carry more exposure.

Which of these do you think is underrated?
Want me to go deeper on any part?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Worth separating 'possible someday' from 'broken today'.

What is the concrete attack he's describing, and how many coins sit in addresses with exposed public keys?
hits.video_tip: Padlock with two shadows labeled AI and quantum, caption 'which one is real?'; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for specifics: which attack, which coins (exposed public keys, reused addresses), and what timeline; avoid fear without evidence.
hits.why_chosen: Open debate with many replies and saves; room for a clarifying, evidence-first reply.

hits.name: Bitcoin Archive
hits.text:
A dip below the 50-week moving average after a sharp rally isn’t necessarily bearish.

Same pattern in 2023, and BTC gained 49% over the next 30 days. https://t.co/jvy590DBJg
hits.hook: A dip below the 50-week moving average after a sharp rally isn’t necessarily bearish.
hits.story: BTC dip below the 50-week MA
hits.draft_en:
'A dip below the 50-week average isn't bearish. Same pattern in 2023, then +49% in 30 days.'

Maybe. But that's one example.

Before trusting a setup:
- how many times did it happen?
- what was the median result, not the best one?
- how many times did it fail?

One chart is a story. A sample is evidence.

Anyone have the full list of 50-week MA breaks for $BTC?
Save this for the next 'same pattern as' chart.
hits.draft_quote_en:
One instance from 2023 isn't a base rate.

How many times has $BTC closed below the 50-week MA after a rally, and what did the next 30 days look like in each case? The median would say more than the best one.
hits.video_tip: Overlay several 50-week MA breaks on one chart, then highlight only 2023 to show cherry-picking; 12s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Turn the n=1 claim into a base rate: list every $BTC close below the 50-week MA after a rally and check the median 30-day return (backtest to run, don't quote a figure).
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + every weekly $BTC close below the 50-week MA after a rally, with the following 30-day return for each case (median marked); price history to be checked. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Single-example pattern claim with big reach; ideal for a base-rate check he can actually run.

hits.name: Coinvo
hits.text:
JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. has warned Gulf allies to prepare for an intense renewal of the Iran war after the midterms.

The warning reportedly covers several Gulf Arab states.

President Trump reportedly plans to hit Iran's nuclear sites and infrastructure once the elections are over. https://t.co/VIV32QJilA
hits.hook: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 U.S. has warned Gulf allies to prepare for an intense renewal of the Iran war after the midterms.
hits.story: Reported US warning to Gulf allies on Iran
hits.draft_en:
"Reportedly" is doing a lot of work in geopolitical headlines.

For a $BTC spot holder, the practical questions:
- is this confirmed by more than one source?
- how did $BTC trade after past escalation headlines?
- does it change your plan, or just your mood?

A rule written in a calm week beats a reaction to a headline.
Save this for the next scary headline.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Single-source "reportedly" story. Worth waiting for confirmation.

And for markets: what did $BTC actually do in the weeks after past escalation headlines? Has anyone checked the base rate instead of guessing?
hits.video_tip: Headline on screen, stamp 'reportedly', then 'what does your rule say?' 8s.
hits.reply_angle: Event-study angle: check BTC returns after past Middle East escalation headlines instead of assuming risk-off; flag it's single-source.
hits.why_chosen: Geopolitical headline with replies and quotes; room for an event-study / base-rate angle without taking sides.

hits.name: Dan Held
hits.text: If your financial advisor hasn't recommended Bitcoin yet, fire them.
hits.hook: If your financial advisor hasn't recommended Bitcoin yet, fire them.
hits.story: Fire your advisor if no Bitcoin
hits.draft_en:
'If your advisor hasn't recommended Bitcoin, fire them.'

I'd ask a different question first:
- did they explain the drawdowns? (check 2018, 2022)
- did they talk about custody?
- did they size it to your situation?

An advisor who says 'buy' without that is worse than one who says 'not yet'.

What would you want them to explain?
Save this before your next advisor meeting.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Recommending it isn't the test. Explaining sizing, drawdowns and custody is.

An advisor who says 'buy' and stops there isn't better.
hits.video_tip: Three-question checklist appearing over an office meeting scene; 10s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Reframe the test: what matters is whether the advisor explains sizing, past drawdowns and custody, not whether they say 'buy'.
hits.why_chosen: Provocative one-liner with lots of replies; easy to add a practical checklist.

hits.name: Anthony Pompliano 🌪
hits.text: The market hates uncertainty, but certainty will return when the midterms are over.
hits.hook: The market hates uncertainty, but certainty will return when the midterms are over.
hits.story: Pompliano: certainty returns after the midterms
hits.draft_en:
'The market hates uncertainty, but certainty will return when the midterms are over.'

Testable claim.

If it's true, volatility should drop after past midterms.
For $BTC we only have a few cycles: 2014, 2018, 2022.

That's a tiny sample. And in 2022 FTX collapsed the same week.

So what do you trust more here, the pattern or the next surprise?
Save this and check it again in mid-November.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Easy to check, at least partly.

What did $BTC realized volatility do in the 30 days after the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms vs the 30 days before? Three cases isn't much, but it beats a feeling.
hits.video_tip: Three mini charts (2014, 2018, 2022) with the election day line and volatility before vs after; 12s.
hits.reply_angle: Test it: compare $BTC 30-day realized volatility before vs after the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms (data to pull) and flag the small sample and the FTX collapse in Nov 2022.
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + $BTC 30-day realized volatility before vs after the 2014, 2018 and 2022 US midterms, election day marked; data to be checked. Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.
hits.why_chosen: Clean, debatable macro claim from a huge account that he can test with a small backtest.

hits.name: Bitcoin.com News
hits.text:
🔐 The weakest link may not be the hacker.

@justinsuntron says many crypto security failures come down to careless habits, not “super sophisticated” attacks and urges 2FA and security keys.

hits.hook: 🔐 The weakest link may not be the hacker.
hits.draft_en:
"Most crypto security failures come from careless habits, not sophisticated attacks."

Plausible. And easy to test on yourself.

Quick audit:
- seed phrase ever typed into a phone or PC?
- SMS 2FA anywhere?
- same email on every exchange?
- $BTC sitting on an exchange you don't trade?

How many did you pass?
Save this and run it once a month.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Agree on habits. The missing number is the split: how much lost BTC came from user error vs custodial failures like hacks or frozen withdrawals?

That tells you whether 2FA or self-custody matters more.
hits.video_tip: Checklist animation, four items ticking or failing, score at the end. 9s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for the split: check how much lost BTC came from user mistakes vs custodian failures (hacks, frozen withdrawals) before ranking fixes.
hits.why_chosen: Asks the reader directly if their setup would pass; easy to answer with a practical checklist.

hits.name: Documenting ₿itcoin 📄
hits.text: How the cryptography of Bitcoin works https://t.co/FrEzkJLJeX
hits.hook: How the cryptography of Bitcoin works https://t.co/FrEzkJLJeX
hits.story: How Bitcoin cryptography works
hits.draft_en:
Most people holding $BTC can't explain what their keys actually do.

You don't need the math. You need three ideas:
- private key: signs
- public key: lets others verify
- seed: the backup of all of it

Lose the seed, lose access.
Share the seed, lose the coins.

What part of custody confused you most at first?
Save this for whoever you're onboarding.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Good one to share.

What's the one cryptography concept you think every self-custody user should understand before buying their first sat?
hits.video_tip: Three cards: key signs, pubkey verifies, seed backs up; 9:16, 12s.

hits.text: Talarico and Trump held competing rallies in Lubbock. Talarico’s rally was nearly twice the size of Trumps. This is the begging of the end for MAGA and it’s happening in the great state of Texas.
hits.hook: Talarico and Trump held competing rallies in Lubbock. Talarico’s rally was nearly twice the size of Trumps. This is the begging of the end for MAGA and it’s happening in the great state of Texas.
hits.story: Rally size as an election signal (Texas)
hits.draft_en:
Crowd size at a rally gets posted as proof of who wins.

It's a weak signal.
Venue, timing, busing and who bothers to show up all distort it.

Same thing happens in markets.
A loud crowd on the timeline isn't the same as money behind the view.

If you had to pick one signal for next week, polls, prediction markets or crowds?
Save this for election night.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Rally size has a long record of fooling people.

If you want a signal with a cost attached, check what prediction markets price for that race and compare it to the polls. Which one moved this week?
hits.video_tip: Three columns, crowds vs polls vs prediction markets, with a check mark that only lands after the result; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Stay non-partisan: rally size is a noisy signal; suggest checking prediction market odds vs polls for that race and how each did in past cycles.
hits.why_chosen: High-reply political claim; bridges to evidence vs vibes and prediction markets without taking a side.

The signal might be the dissents.

For $BTC spot holders, the useful question:
- does a hold move price a week later?
- or is it noise around a trend?

I'd check the base rate before reacting.

If it was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Two votes for a hike says more than the hold itself.

Has $BTC behaved differently after meetings with hawkish dissents? That would be worth checking before reading anything into today.

hits.story: Bitwise $1.6M BTC target by 2036
hits.draft_en:
Bitwise raised its $BTC target to $1.6M by 2036, per The Block.

A 10-year price target is a model, not a forecast you can check soon.

What matters is the inputs:
- how much institutions allocate
- how fast that happens
- what supply is actually liquid

Change one input and the number moves a lot.

Which assumption do you trust least?
If this helps you read the next target, a repost spreads it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
The interesting part isn't $1.6M, it's the allocation assumption behind it.

What does the model give if institutions allocate half of what Bitwise assumes? Is that scenario published?
hits.video_tip: Slider animation: change the allocation assumption and watch the 2036 target swing; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Ask for the sensitivity: which allocation and adoption inputs drive the $1.6M, and what the target is if they come in at half (check the Bitwise report).
hits.visual_suggestion: Visual sugerido: [chart] + scenario bars for the 2036 target under different institutional allocation assumptions, taken only from the Bitwise report (to be checked). Account style: navy blue background, Bitcoin in white, lime accents, logo watermark.

This is the right way to answer a bet: check the claim, not the vibes.

Google searches for Bitcoin at a 5-year low while $BTC sits near $80K, per a post going around today.

'Still early' is one read.
Another: retail attention lags price, and low interest can last.

Search interest is a sentiment gauge, not a timing tool.

What I'd check:
- past lows in search interest
- $BTC 6 and 12 months later
- how often low interest stayed low

Save this for the next time someone says 'still early'.
hits.draft_quote_en:
5-year low in searches, per the post. Does low search interest have a track record as a buy signal, or does it just mean retail isn't watching?

Would like to see the past lows and what $BTC did 6 and 12 months after.
hits.video_tip: Search-interest line falling while price stays flat, caption 'early or ignored?'; 10s.

hits.story: Money since 1971
hits.draft_en:
'We haven't had money since 1971.'

It's a common line. Worth splitting into parts:
- 1971 ended dollar convertibility to gold: fact
- prices rose a lot since: fact
- 'pyramid scheme': interpretation

You can argue the system favors asset holders without calling it fraud.
The first claim is easier to defend with data.

Which part do you think holds up best?
Save this for the next 1971 thread.
hits.draft_quote_en:
The 1971 break is real. 'Pyramid scheme' is a big jump from it.

What would the evidence look like? Wealth share by percentile since 1971 would be a start.
hits.video_tip: Timeline card: 1944, 1971, today, with 'fact' and 'interpretation' labels popping in; 10s.
hits.reply_angle: Separate fact from interpretation: 1971 is a fact, 'pyramid scheme' is a claim; suggest checking wealth share by percentile since 1971 before concluding.
hits.why_chosen: Strong, debatable claim with good engagement; easy to add fact vs. interpretation.
